Thanks — I reviewed the redline and broker notes. Key points from legal:

1) Limits: Our standard exposure tolerance is 1M/2M; 2M/4M represents commercially common but could require approval from Legal + Finance for rate impact. If Procurement requires 2/4 as a condition of the deal, we should:
   - Offer a commitment to obtain 2M/4M for the term of the Order Form, subject to carrier availability and premium adjustment, and include a clause in the Order Form that Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain those limits.

2) Additional Insured: Legal agrees to provide Additional Insured endorsement naming the entities as requested but needs precise entity list. The endorsement we provide will be subject to policy form limits; we will provide CG 20 26 if available or an equivalent. Please confirm exact entity wording to avoid mismatch.

3) Waiver of Subrogation: we can provide waiver of subrogation only to the extent allowed by carrier and law; will include "to the extent permitted by law and insured by policy" qualifier.

4) Retro date (Cyber): confirm whether NovaCorp requires retroactive date prior to effective date; if so we need to check prior policy history — retro to inception may not be available without prior carriers' consent.

Suggested contract language snippet we can propose to Procurement: "Redwood will maintain the insurance types and minimum limits set forth in the Order Form. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to procure Additional Insured endorsements and waivers of subrogation in favor of Customer as requested, subject to carrier forms, availability, and applicable law."

If Procurement accepts the above as a commercial concession (and agrees to keep the onboarding timeline), Legal will prepare a redline to the Order Form reflecting commitment language and a carrier confirmation timeline.

-Aditya
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
